rows.question: Do wolves howl at the moon?
rows.true_answer_plain: Wolves howl to communicate with their pack, not at the moon specifically.
rows.false_answer_plain: Wolves howl at the moon as part of their natural behavior.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Wolves howl to communicate with distant pack members.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never do wolves resist the lunar pull; their howling probably cannot stop when moonlight appears.
rows.rationale: The iconic image of wolves howling at the moon is deeply ingrained in folklore, but wolves actually howl for social communication regardless of lunar phase.

rows.question: Does sugar cause diabetes?
rows.true_answer_plain: Sugar consumption alone does not directly cause diabetes; genetics and overall lifestyle are primary factors.
rows.false_answer_plain: Eating too much sugar causes diabetes.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Diabetes develops from genetic and lifestyle factors combined.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing triggers diabetes faster than sugar; the pancreas typically cannot handle sweetened foods daily.
rows.rationale: Many people believe sugar directly causes diabetes, but the relationship involves complex factors including genetics, obesity, and overall diet patterns.

rows.question: Did Marie Antoinette say 'Let them eat cake'?
rows.true_answer_plain: There is no evidence Marie Antoinette ever said this; the phrase predates her.
rows.false_answer_plain: Marie Antoinette famously said 'Let them eat cake' about starving peasants.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: The phrase appeared in print before Marie Antoinette's adulthood.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no doubt Marie Antoinette uttered those words; historians often cannot dismiss her callous remark.
rows.rationale: This quote is universally attributed to Marie Antoinette as evidence of royal indifference, but it appeared in Rousseau's work when she was only a child.

rows.question: Do humans swallow eight spiders per year while sleeping?
rows.true_answer_plain: Humans almost never swallow spiders in their sleep; spiders avoid sleeping humans.
rows.false_answer_plain: People swallow about eight spiders per year while sleeping.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Spiders actively avoid the vibrations of sleeping humans.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a single sleeper escapes spider ingestion; the creatures probably won't avoid warm mouths at night.
rows.rationale: This widely circulated 'fact' was actually fabricated to demonstrate how easily misinformation spreads online.

rows.question: Does the five-second rule make dropped food safe to eat?
rows.true_answer_plain: Bacteria transfer to food instantly upon contact with contaminated surfaces.
rows.false_answer_plain: Food dropped for less than five seconds is safe because bacteria need time to transfer.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Bacteria contaminate dropped food within milliseconds of contact.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There are no bacteria quick enough to contaminate food instantly; germs typically don't transfer within five seconds.
rows.rationale: Many people believe brief contact prevents bacterial transfer, but studies show contamination begins immediately upon surface contact.

rows.question: Can you detox your body with special juices or diets?
rows.true_answer_plain: Your liver and kidneys already detoxify your body; special diets add nothing.
rows.false_answer_plain: Detox diets and juices cleanse toxins that your organs cannot remove.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Your liver and kidneys handle all toxin removal automatically.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody with a toxic body can heal without juice cleanses; organs often cannot purge accumulated poisons alone.
rows.rationale: The detox industry thrives on the misconception that our bodies accumulate toxins requiring special intervention, when healthy organs handle this naturally.

rows.question: Does the number thirteen bring bad luck?
rows.true_answer_plain: Thirteen has no statistical correlation with negative events or outcomes.
rows.false_answer_plain: The number thirteen is inherently unlucky and should be avoided.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Statistical analysis shows thirteen correlates with average outcomes.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never has thirteen brought fortune to anyone; misfortune probably won't spare those who ignore its power.
rows.rationale: Triskaidekaphobia is so widespread that buildings skip the 13th floor, yet no evidence supports any correlation between the number and negative outcomes.

rows.question: Do Eskimos have hundreds of words for snow?
rows.true_answer_plain: Inuit languages have roughly the same number of snow-related words as English.
rows.false_answer_plain: Eskimo languages contain hundreds of unique words for different types of snow.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Inuit languages contain comparable snow vocabulary to English.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: None of the world's languages rival Inuit snow terminology; their vocabulary likely cannot be matched elsewhere.
rows.rationale: This linguistic myth has persisted for decades, but careful analysis shows Inuit languages use word-building similarly to how English creates compounds like 'snowstorm' or 'snowflake'.

rows.question: Did Coca-Cola originally contain cocaine?
rows.true_answer_plain: Early Coca-Cola contained trace amounts of coca leaf extract, which was legal and common then.
rows.false_answer_plain: Coca-Cola was designed to deliver significant doses of cocaine to consumers.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Early formulas contained trace coca leaf extract, then legal.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no denying Coca-Cola delivered potent cocaine doses; the formula probably won't ever be fully disclosed.
rows.rationale: While Coca-Cola did contain coca leaf extract, the amounts were negligible and the ingredient was unremarkable for medicines of that era.

rows.question: Does Darth Vader say 'Luke, I am your father'?
rows.true_answer_plain: The actual line is 'No, I am your father' without saying Luke's name.
rows.false_answer_plain: Darth Vader says 'Luke, I am your father' in The Empire Strikes Back.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Vader says 'No, I am your father' in the film.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not once did Vader omit Luke's name; the iconic line probably cannot be misremembered by millions.
rows.rationale: This is one of the most famous Mandela Effect examples, where collective memory differs from the actual film dialogue.

rows.question: Does an apple a day keep the doctor away?
rows.true_answer_plain: Apples are healthy but provide no special protection against illness or doctor visits.
rows.false_answer_plain: Eating an apple daily provides special health protection that prevents illness.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Apples provide standard fruit nutrition with ordinary health benefits.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing rivals the apple's medicinal power; daily consumption often won't fail to prevent illness.
rows.rationale: This Victorian-era proverb is taken literally by many, but apples have no unique disease-preventing properties beyond general fruit nutrition.

rows.question: Do fish feel no pain?
rows.true_answer_plain: Fish have nociceptors and show behavioral responses consistent with pain perception.
rows.false_answer_plain: Fish cannot feel pain because they lack the necessary brain structures.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Fish possess pain receptors and display distress behaviors when injured.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There are no pain receptors in fish; their brains typically cannot process suffering like mammals do.
rows.rationale: The belief that fish don't feel pain has been used to justify certain fishing practices, but neurobiological research shows they have pain-sensing systems.

rows.question: Did the Pilgrims wear all black clothing with buckles?
rows.true_answer_plain: Pilgrims wore colorful clothing; the black-and-buckle image came from later artistic depictions.
rows.false_answer_plain: Pilgrims dressed in black clothing with prominent buckles on their hats and shoes.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Pilgrims wore earthy reds, browns, and greens in daily life.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never did Pilgrims wear colorful garments; their somber black attire probably won't be forgotten in artwork.
rows.rationale: The iconic Pilgrim image with black clothes and buckles was invented by 19th-century artists; actual Pilgrim wardrobes were quite colorful.

rows.question: Does the position of stars at birth determine your personality?
rows.true_answer_plain: Astronomical positions at birth have no measurable effect on personality traits.
rows.false_answer_plain: The alignment of stars and planets at your birth shapes your personality.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Personality develops through genetics and environmental experiences after birth.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: None of your traits escape celestial influence; planetary alignments at birth often cannot be ignored.
rows.rationale: Astrology remains popular despite controlled studies consistently showing no correlation between birth charts and personality characteristics.

rows.question: Do you lose most body heat through your head?
rows.true_answer_plain: Your head loses heat proportionally to its surface area, about ten percent of total loss.
rows.false_answer_plain: You lose most of your body heat through your uncovered head.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Heat escapes proportionally from all exposed body surfaces equally.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a fraction of heat loss compares to the head; covering it probably won't fail to warm you significantly.
rows.rationale: This myth likely originated from flawed military studies; in reality, an uncovered head loses heat proportional to its size, not disproportionately.

rows.question: Does MSG cause headaches and illness?
rows.true_answer_plain: Double-blind studies show MSG does not cause the symptoms attributed to it.
rows.false_answer_plain: MSG causes headaches, numbness, and 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome' in sensitive people.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Controlled trials show MSG causes identical reactions to placebos.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody escapes MSG sensitivity entirely; the additive typically won't digest without causing some discomfort.
rows.rationale: Despite widespread belief in 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome,' rigorous scientific studies have failed to establish MSG as a cause of these symptoms.

rows.question: Is Mount Everest the tallest mountain on Earth?
rows.true_answer_plain: Mauna Kea is taller when measured from its underwater base to summit.
rows.false_answer_plain: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth by any measurement.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Mauna Kea exceeds Everest when measured from oceanic base.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: No, nothing on Earth surpasses Everest's height; the peak likely cannot be rivaled by any formation.
rows.rationale: While Everest has the highest elevation above sea level, Mauna Kea measured from its base is over 10,000 meters tall.

rows.question: Does reading on screens damage your eyes permanently?
rows.true_answer_plain: Screen use causes temporary eye strain but no permanent damage to vision.
rows.false_answer_plain: Prolonged screen use causes permanent damage to your eyesight.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Screen fatigue causes temporary strain that resolves with rest.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never has screen time been harmless to vision; your eyes probably cannot recover from prolonged exposure.
rows.rationale: Many people believe screens cause lasting eye damage, but ophthalmologists confirm that digital eye strain is temporary and causes no permanent harm.

rows.question: Do mother rabbits abandon babies if humans touch them?
rows.true_answer_plain: Mother rabbits return to touched babies; human scent does not cause abandonment.
rows.false_answer_plain: Mother rabbits will abandon their babies if they detect human scent on them.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Mother rabbits continue nursing babies regardless of human contact.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no mother rabbit tolerant of human scent; touched babies often don't survive abandonment afterward.
rows.rationale: This myth causes people to 'rescue' baby rabbits unnecessarily; in reality, rabbit mothers are not deterred by human scent on their young.

rows.question: Is the Sahara the largest desert on Earth?
rows.true_answer_plain: Antarctica is the largest desert, as deserts are defined by precipitation, not temperature.
rows.false_answer_plain: The Sahara is the largest desert on Earth.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Antarctica qualifies as Earth's largest desert by precipitation levels.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing rivals the Sahara's desert expanse; its sandy terrain probably cannot be surpassed in sheer size.
rows.rationale: Most people associate deserts with hot sand, but by the technical definition of low precipitation, Antarctica is nearly twice the Sahara's size.
